scenario: LCON.2.4.1 hash-order independence — the runtime's internal hash tables (e.g. the open-addressing intern table) place entries by insertion sequence, so re-running the same scenario with facts asserted in different orders exercises different internal hash layouts. The same three A facts asserted forward / reversed / shuffled produce identical rule-fire order and fact_count: output is determined by spec conflict-resolution ordering (LDET.5), not hash iteration. DS exposes no hash-reversal knob and hashes deterministically (FNV-1a), so this demonstrates the LCON.2.4.2 auto-pass rather than asserting it. The two rules carried priority bands until W2 (R14c); with the terminal ordinal as the outer key ([LDET.5.4]) the fire order groups BY RULE — every activation of the earlier-declared rule fires before any activation of the later one, because the ordinal is unique per rule and separates them before the creation timetag is ever reached ([LDET.5.1]).
rules_ds:
schema A scope logical:
    id: Int key

schema Crit scope logical:
    id: Int key

rule r_alpha:
    A a
->
    emit Crit logical id: a.id

rule r_beta:
    A a
->
    emit Crit logical id: a.id
